_comment: Merged into ~/.claude/settings.json by install.sh. Only permissions.allow and permissions.deny are read from here; hooks are generated by the installer so paths stay correct if this repo moves. Everything else in settings.json is left untouched.
_allow_rationale: Read-only and routine build commands, pre-approved so prompts stay rare and the guard hook is the thing you actually notice. Nothing here mutates remote state or touches credentials.
_allow_overlap_note: These globs overlap the guard hook's read-only pre-approval, deliberately. A glob matches as a prefix over the WHOLE command string, so it can only ever cover simple one-segment commands — 'cd x && cat y' matches nothing here no matter how long this list grows. The hook is what handles compound commands. This list is the fallback for sessions where hooks do not load (--bare), where its worst case is an extra prompt. Note that 'Bash(foo *)' does not match a bare 'foo': the '*' needs something after it, which is why the paired bare forms below exist.

permissions._deny_rationale: Belt to the hook's braces. The mode-guard hook is the real enforcement (it sees full command text and can explain itself); these globs are a cheap second layer in case the hook is ever unloaded — note that --bare skips hooks entirely.
